'''''Chaetachme''''' is a monotypic genus of flowering plants native to eastern and western Africa, including [[Madagascar]],<ref name="jstor">{{Cite web|url=http://plants.jstor.org/search?plantName=Chaetacme%20aristata|title=JSTOR Global Plants: Search Results|website=plants.jstor.org|language=en|access-date=2017-08-01}}</ref> containing the single species '''''Chaetachme aristata'''''. Its [[English language|English]] common name is '''thorny elm''',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.safaripatrol.com/species_trees.shtml |title=Trees & Shrubs of East Africa|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180408185058/http://safaripatrol.com/species_trees.shtml |archive-date=2018-04-08|website=Safari Patrol}}</ref> and it is known as '''''muyuyu''''' in [[Gikuyu language|Kikuyu]].<ref name="fao">{{Cite web|url=http://www.fao.org/docrep/u8995e/u8995e0b.htm|title=Glossary|website=www.fao.org|access-date=2017-08-01}}</ref> Traditionally placed in the [[Ulmaceae|Elm family]], it is more recently placed in the family [[Cannabaceae]], thought to be possibly closely related to ''[[Celtis]]''.

''Chaetachme aristata'' is a [[shrub]] or small [[tree]] growing up to {{convert|10|m}} tall. It has drooping, angular branches covered with [[Thorns, spines, and prickles|spines]] up to {{convert|3.5|cm}} in length. The lance-shaped leaves are up to {{convert|11|cm}} long by {{convert|5|cm}} wide, pointed at the tip and smooth or serrated on the edges. The shrub is [[Plant sexuality|dioecious]] and [[sexual dimorphism|sexually dimorphic]], with male and female flower types borne on separate individuals,<ref name=jstor/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://celp.org.uk/webpages/projects/ecology/forest%20reserves/pdf/Arusha.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110813081852/http://celp.org.uk/webpages/projects/ecology/forest%20reserves/pdf/Arusha.pdf |archive-date=2011-08-13|title=The management and ecology of Tanzanian forests {{!}} Arusha Region}}</ref> although it may also be [[monoecious]].<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.12705/623.9|title=Molecular phylogenetics and character evolution of Cannabaceae|year=2013|last1=Yang|first1=Mei-Qing|last2=Van Velzen|first2=Robin|last3=Bakker|first3=Freek T.|last4=Sattarian|first4=Ali|last5=Li|first5=De-Zhu|last6=Yi|first6=Ting-Shuang|journal=Taxon|volume=62|issue=3|pages=473–485}}</ref>

This shrub is host to the [[Miridae|mirid bug]] ''[[Volumnus chaetacme]]''.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Linnavuori, R. |year=1996|url=http://research.amnh.org/pbi/library/4950.pdf|title=Taxonomic studies of the Miridae (Heteroptera) of Africa and the Middle East|journal=Acta Universitatis Carolinae Biologica|volume=40|pages=321–350}}</ref>

The spiny branches of the shrub are used as [[fence]]s in African villages.<ref name=fao/><ref>{{cite journal|author=Bussmann, R. W.|display-authors=et al|year=2006 |title=Plant use of the Maasai of Sekenani Valley, Maasai Mara, Kenya|journal=J Ethnobiol Ethnomed|volume=2|page=22|doi=10.1186/1746-4269-2-22 |doi-access=free |pmid=16674830 |pmc=1475560 }}</ref>
